newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia's Victoria says debt upgrade warranted.
newsitem.headline: Australia's Victoria says debt upgrade warranted.

text.p: The Victoria state government said on Tuesday that the conditions were right for an upgrade of its long-term domestic credit rating to AAA from the current rating of AA-plus as set by Standard and Poor's Corp.

Speaking after announcing the sale of the government's Loy Yang A power station and coal mine for A$4.746 billion, state Treasurer Alan Stockdale said the debt market was already treating Victorian debt as triple-A stock.
"We believe the conditions for an upgrade are in place," Stockdale said.

S&P affirmed the domestic long-term and short-term ratings of AA-plus and A1-plus on March 11, citing the state's signficant reduction in its debt burden due to large privatisations and the state's broad economic base.
The long term rating was upgraded from AA on September 12 last year, with Stockdale saying at the time that Victoria hoped for a triple-A rating by the year 2000.
Moody's Investors Service upgraded Victoria's domestic rating to AA1 from AA2 on December 23 last year, again citing the state's debt burden recovery.
